Name: Pokemon Eggventure - Pokedex
Author: Parme69
Description:
[center][size=6][b]Pokemon Eggventure — Pokedex[/b][/size][/center]

[center][i]You asked for it. Here it is.[/i][/center]

An in-game Pokedex that fills itself in as you raise Pokemon. No list to tick, no second window beside the game, nothing to set up.

[line]

[size=5][b]The Professor sends it to you[/b][/size]

The morning after you raise your first Pokemon, a letter arrives. Professor Oak has heard about your farm and sends you a device of his own making.

Hold it, use it, and the Pokedex opens. There is a keyboard shortcut too, for anyone who would rather keep the hotbar free.

[line]

[size=5][b]Every stage, not just the first[/b][/size]

The Pokedex lists close to [b]1200 entries[/b]: every species Pokemon Eggventure can give you, [b]plus each stage of its evolution line[/b].

Entries are grouped [b]by family[/b] rather than strictly by number, so Cleffa, Clefairy and Clefable sit side by side even though their National Dex numbers are far apart.

A stage you have never raised stays a dark silhouette. An evolution unlocks the day one of your Pokemon actually reaches it — no shortcuts, and changing an animal's look with the scissors will not fool it.

[line]

[size=5][b]Hover over anything[/b][/size]

Everything is on the tooltip. There is no panel to open and close.

[list]
[*][b]National Dex number[/b], name and [b]type[/b]
[*][b]Habitat[/b] — coop or barn — and its [b]incubation time[/b], which follows your own config settings
[*][b]Height and weight[/b], and the species' official Pokedex entry
[*][b]Resources[/b] — every item it gives you, shown with icons: produce, daily held item, its own egg
[*][b]Biome[/b] — where to find it, with the details: which mine floors, which festival, which forage area
[*][b]When[/b] — the season or weather, whenever the source has one
[*][b]First met[/b] — the very day it entered your Pokedex
[*][b]Ring[/b] — whether you already own its Follow Me ring
[/list]
Each Pokemon [b]calls out[/b] as your cursor passes over it.

[line]

[size=5][b]Finding what you want[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Search by name or number.[/b] Accents are ignored — typing "Ecremeuh" finds "Écrémeuh".
[*][b]Eighteen type filters.[/b] Hover a tab to see how far along you are with that type.
[*][b]Obtained / Missing.[/b] Two buttons to show only what you have, or only what is left.
[*][b]My hunt.[/b] Right-click any Pokemon to mark it as a target, then filter down to your list.
[*][b]NEW badges[/b] on anything you have not looked at yet, cleared as you hover them.
[/list]
Every morning, one grouped message tells you what joined the Pokedex overnight.

[line]

[size=5][b]Shiny Charms[/b][/size]

Raise every Pokemon of a single type — legendaries aside — and the Professor sends you that type's [b]Shiny Charm[/b].

From then on, shiny Pokemon of that type hatch [b]three times as often[/b]. There are eighteen charms to earn, and nothing to carry around: the charm works from the moment it is yours.

[line]

[size=5][b]Details that matter[/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Shared in multiplayer.[/b] What one farmhand raises counts for everyone.
[*][b]Controller and keyboard.[/b] The whole menu can be used without a mouse.
[*][b]Fits your screen.[/b] The grid grows on a large display and still fits on a small one.
[*][b]Seven settings[/b] through Generic Mod Config Menu, including whether unknown Pokemon reveal their biome — off by default, so the hunt stays a hunt.
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][b]It stays out of your way[/b][/size]

This is a [b]separate, optional[/b] mod. Pokemon Eggventure works exactly as before without it, and removing it leaves nothing behind.

It reads the pack rather than copying it: a species added to Pokemon Eggventure appears in the Pokedex on its own.

[line]

[size=5][b]Requirements[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]SMAPI
[*]Pokemon Eggventure 2.1.0 or later
[/list]
[b]Optional:[/b] Generic Mod Config Menu to change settings in game, and Pokemon Eggventure — Follow Me if you want the ring line on the tooltip.

[line]

[size=5][b]Languages[/b][/size]

English and French, including type names, the Professor's letters and the Pokemon names themselves.

[line]

[center][i]Thank you to everyone who asked for this one. It was the most requested feature by far.[/i][/center]
